source.anchor_kjv: And the word of the LORD came unto him, saying, Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee. So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink. And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand. And she said, As the LORD thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die. And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Elijah.
source.hook_line: A widow was gathering sticks for her own funeral fire.
source.spoken_script: A widow was gathering sticks for her own funeral fire. A stranger passing through, Elijah, asked her for water. Then bread. She had nothing to spare — nothing, period: "I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse... that we may eat it, and die." Elijah answered: "Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son." She fed a stranger before she fed her own child. The barrel of meal wasted not. The oil did not fail, for as long as the famine lasted. Centuries later, Jesus named her by her own city: "Many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias... but unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow." Of every hungry house in Israel, God went to the one with nothing left to give — and asked her anyway. She didn't have enough. She gave first anyway. The barrel that fed a stranger fed her too — it never once ran dry. God doesn't need your barrel full. He needs it open.

platforms.title: The Widow Who Fed a Stranger Before Her Own Starving Son
platforms.description:
1 Kings 17:8-16: a widow in Zarephath was gathering two sticks to cook one last meal before she and her son died of famine. A stranger, the prophet Elijah, asked her first for water, then for bread.

She told him honestly: "I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die."

Elijah answered: "Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth."

She fed a stranger before she fed her own child. The barrel of meal wasted not. The oil did not fail, for as long as the famine lasted.

Centuries later, in his own hometown synagogue, Jesus named her by her city, the one widow in all Israel that Elijah was sent to. Of every hungry house in the land, God went to the one with nothing left to give, and asked her anyway.

She did not have enough. She gave first anyway. God did not need her barrel full. He needed it open.
